LESSON: GRAMMAR IN USE 8.3.1 SENTENCES

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 8
Topic 8.3: Grammar in Use 8.3.1 Sentences

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Grammar in Use 8.3.1 Sentences. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: What are some of your school rules?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify questions tags and double imperatives from a text
2. use question tags and double imperatives correctly in sentences

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: GRAMMAR IN USE 8.3.1 SENTENCES
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE · Grade: Grade 5
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Grammar in Use 8.3.1 Sentences helps you succeed in ENGLISH LANGUAGE. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: GRAMMAR IN USE 8.3.1 SENTENCES
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify questions tags and double imperatives from a text

What this means
In this part you learn to identify questions tags and double imperatives from a text. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify questions tags and double imperatives from a text.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Grammar in Use 8.3.1 Sentences”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify questions tags and double imperatives from a text. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Use question tags and double imperatives correctly in sentences

What this means
In this part you learn to use question tags and double imperatives correctly in sentences. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: use question tags and double imperatives correctly in sentences.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Grammar in Use 8.3.1 Sentences to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can use question tags and double imperatives correctly in sentences. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Grammar in Use 8.3.1 Sentences is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Grammar in Use 8.3.1 Sentences”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify questions tags and double imperatives from a text)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Grammar in Use 8.3.1 Sentences to a partner. (skill: use question tags and double imperatives correctly in sentences)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Grammar in Use 8.3.1 Sentences to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify questions tags and double imperatives from a text.
3. Practise this skill: use question tags and double imperatives correctly in sentences.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Grammar in Use 8.3.1 Sentences from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Grammar in Use 8.3.1 Sentences: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 5 learner study Grammar in Use 8.3.1 Sentences?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. What are some of your school rules?
2. How do you give instructions?
3. Why do we ask questions?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Grammar in Use 8.3.1 Sentences means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify questions tags and double imperatives from a text.
5. Be able to: use question tags and double imperatives correctly in sentences.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
